entries.note: The absolute contrast is a polemical characterization of Huang's value.
Whether an industry 'makes sense' has no shared factual test.

entries.test: Public records of NVIDIA's supply expectations, investor statements and prior conduct, together with applicable securities standards, would test the allegation of repeated stock manipulation.
entries.note: The legal disclaimer and 'feels like' qualify an allegation about concrete conduct.
The infrastructure history is testable, but 'far more foundational' supplies no shared way to rank the participants' contributions.

entries.test: Contemporaneous financial reporting and market commentary would show whether AI was routinely credited for essentially all related revenue growth among NVIDIA GPU buyers.
entries.note: The insults do not erase the observable claim about coverage and attribution.

entries.test: NVIDIA's demand statements, investments, recipients' borrowing and subsequent GPU purchases would establish whether its funding inflated the demand it advertised.
entries.note: The central allegation links NVIDIA's financing to demand creation.
The same paragraph immediately supplies AI revenue figures, making 'nowhere to be seen' an exaggeration.

entries.test: GPU orders, supply allocations and customer financing records would show whether the advertised excess demand depended on Huang's pressure tactics and NVIDIA-funded purchases.
entries.note: The omitted SPV transaction is an example of the retained causal allegation.

entries.test: Inventory valuations, installation records and purchasing terms would show whether over $200 billion of NVIDIA GPUs awaited installation because of NVIDIA's demand pressures.
entries.note: 'I believe' introduces a supported factual assertion here, rather than an explicit chance or possibility.

entries.test: The August analysis, underlying analyst estimates and subsequent public discussion would test the demand shares and whether the findings were ignored.
entries.note: The normalization omits his explanation that people ignored the findings because they were uncomfortable.

entries.test: Customer orders and financing histories would show whether all the demand competitors might capture originated in Huang's deals and NVIDIA's financial support.
entries.note: He rejects the competitors' opportunity and endorses the causal premise; he does not endorse the quoted possibility.

entries.test: Coverage of NVIDIA-related circular deals would show whether every deal received uncritical approval tied to headline dollar amounts without discussion of instability or inflated revenues.
entries.note: The normalization drops the qualification that the money could be unreal and its specified NVIDIA-related source.
He presents tightening conditions and an approaching end as suggestions drawn from the warnings.
The numbers do not define what constitutes the bubble's inflation or collapse.

entries.test: AI compute providers' customer sales and usage disclosures would establish whether Anthropic and OpenAI account for the vast majority of AI compute sold.
entries.note: Customer concentration has a plain empirical reading despite the approximate threshold.

entries.test: Customer revenue concentration disclosures, purchasers' financial results and investment records would test the 80%/1% concentration, startup losses and NVIDIA funding.
entries.note: The necessary customer data need not already be public for the claim to be checkable.
Calling buying and renting bad deals evaluates their worth without specifying a financial test.
The full claim attributes nondisclosure to a private motive. Spending and revenue figures are separately checkable.

entries.test: Microsoft's quarterly revenue disclosures and public reporting on OpenAI's losses and financing would test the stated shares, revenue trend, losses, funding and valuation.
entries.note: The revenue-decline inference is tentative, but the sentence also makes multiple firm numerical assertions.

entries.test: Hyperscalers' capacity utilization, construction commitments and NVIDIA purchasing arrangements would show whether they overbuilt primarily because of Huang's pressure.
entries.note: The possibility of filling the gap is a concession; the overbuilding and causal attribution are asserted firmly.

entries.test: AI startup revenue totals, company financial results and compute contracts would test the 89% share, losses and existing seven-year spending commitments and funding dependencies.
entries.note: The opening is evaluative, but its numerical premises are firm and testable. Existing commitments can be checked before the spending occurs.

entries.test: Startup financing histories, revenue and cash-flow reports, and GPU rental expenses would test whether rental costs force the stated fundraising amounts and frequency.
entries.note: The efficiency clause is hedged, while the financing pattern and its alleged cause are asserted.

entries.test: NVIDIA's leadership records, financing policies and new investments or guarantees would show whether Huang's role and NVIDIA's support for dependent companies had ended.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives the bubble metaphor a concrete claim about the cessation of financing support.

entries.test: Representative willingness-to-pay surveys and compute customers' financial and payment records would test whether overwhelming majorities reject paying for AI or cannot afford their compute purchases.
entries.note: Population preferences and financial affordability can be assessed through public empirical evidence.
'All that anybody can think about' exaggerates the attention a slowdown would attract.
